leads.summary: Unsatisfiable dependency is not evidence of IgnorePkg, but the new diagnostic presents it as a fact
leads.consequence: An installed foreign/AUR package can require the old version of a dependency while the repo offers an upgrade. Pacman reports exactly the same stderr verdict and :: detail with no IgnorePkg anywhere. The update stops, tells the user a package is held in /etc/pacman.conf and suggests changing holds, which cannot resolve this case. The error repeats next update; an incorrect hold may create a partial upgrade. Report the actual dependency line, qualify the IgnorePkg explanation as one possibility, and distinguish held vs foreign packages before prescribing a remedy.

leads.summary: Open #9070 removes the exact handler and replaces its caller, so the two unstacked PRs cannot coexist unchanged
leads.consequence: #9070 deliberately removes this handler and tests its absence; #11692 adds its whole feature there. If #9070 merges first, #11692 must reimplement diagnostics in the caller or be dropped. If #11692 merges first, #9070 must explicitly preserve or consciously remove the new diagnostic. These are conflicting designs, not two harmless textual overlaps.

limits: No pacman -Syu was run because review.py's sandbox is unprivileged; the -Sup reproduction uses only isolated --config/--root/--dbpath/--cachedir/--gpgdir/--logfile and a file:// repository. The initial -Syu stderr predicate is corroborated by shipped pacman source sync.c:770-785, not a root transaction fixture.

flags.claim: A stub that also prints an `error:` line on stderr and a non-`::` line on stdout would pin the filter.
flags.why: A stub change alone pins nothing. The new case only asserts that the `::` detail and 'IgnorePkg' are present (head test file, lines 293-296). With the filter and `2>/dev/null` removed, an extra non-`::` line and a second `error:` line would be printed, but no assertion checks for their absence. The `error:` line is already in the captured err file because the caller does `cat "$errors" >&2` (bin/omarchy-update-system-pkgs:31). The stub also needs a matching assertion: that the err file does not contain the non-`::` stdout line, and, for the stderr discard, that the stub's distinct stderr line does not appear. My own final report contains the same overstatement.

flags.claim: print the hold advice only when `pacman-conf IgnorePkg` or `IgnoreGroup` lists something, naming them; otherwise suggest rebuilding a foreign package or retrying after mirrors sync.
flags.why: The command and rule are correct (pacman-conf.c:373-376 lists IgnorePkg and IgnoreGroup). But the suggestion implies that gating on configured holds is enough. Two parts of my suggestion were dropped. (1) The hold advice must be worded for either direction: the same section says the paragraph describes the reverse case when the held package is the dependency (S5), and gating alone does not fix that, because in S5 a hold exists and the current paragraph would still print. (2) 'or remove' a foreign package. Neither is an error, but as written the suggestion leaves the S5 problem the draft itself raises unaddressed.

Verified in this check: #9070 deletes bin/omarchy-update-system-pkgs-when-conflicted (115 lines) and rewrites the caller. My final report wrongly called #9070 'stale ... not material' and did not notice the deletion, so my report is internally inconsistent with the draft here. The draft drops a relevant qualifier: #9070 does not merge cleanly into the current quattro tip (GitHub mergeable=false; my merge-tree of quattro+#9070 alone conflicts in bin/omarchy-update-system-pkgs and four other files), and its last commit is from 2026-08-30. Without that qualifier, readers may think #9070 is about to land and supersede this PR.

flags.claim: #13538, #13601 and #9285 each insert at the same point in this handler
flags.why: #13538 and #9285 insert new blocks at that point. #13601 inserts nothing there: it rewrites the comment and leftover-parse lines that start at that point (hunk @@ -81,22 +81,30 @@, replacing 'Paths one of these packages installs...'). The textual-conflict conclusion is correct for all three.

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** The new branch blames an `IgnorePkg` hold for every unsatisfiable dependency, held or not.

### IgnorePkg advice printed with no hold

pacman gives the same verdict, often with the same `::` line, without a hold: a repository that has not rebuilt a dependent yet (likely in #11086), a foreign package built on the old library, or a missing dependency. With real pacman 7.1 and no `IgnorePkg`, the handler still prints the hold text; when the held package is the dependency (a Qt pin as in #8438), it describes the reverse case. **Impact:** same exit status, but misleading advice, and "every system upgrade stops here" is untrue for repository lag.

**Suggested change:** print hold advice only when `pacman-conf IgnorePkg`/`IgnoreGroup` lists something, naming them and worded for either direction; else suggest rebuilding or removing a foreign package, or retrying after mirrors sync.

<details><summary>Reproducer (fails at 19454b8)</summary>

## Reproducer: the IgnorePkg advice is printed when nothing is held

Reviewed head: `19454b84417b1adad09044a3512ac95b57862fba`.

### 1. Test case in the PR's own test file

Append this case to `test/shell.d/update-file-conflict-test.sh` and run `bash test/shell.d/update-file-conflict-test.sh`. It gives the handler the same verdict and the same `::` line as the PR's own case, but with no `IgnorePkg` or `IgnoreGroup` configured (a `pacman-conf` stub that lists nothing).

```bash
# pacman gives the same verdict, and the same "installing X breaks dependency"
# line, when nothing is held: a repository that has not rebuilt hyprland yet
# (issue #11086), or a foreign package built against the old library. With no
# IgnorePkg configured, the report must not tell the user to drop a hold.
cat >"$stub_bin/pacman-conf" <<'STUB'
#!/bin/bash
[[ $1 == IgnorePkg || $1 == IgnoreGroup ]] && exit 0
exit 1
STUB
chmod +x "$stub_bin/pacman-conf"
fresh_work
echo 0 >"$test_tmp/attempts"
echo "error: failed to prepare transaction (could not satisfy dependencies)" >"$test_tmp/report"
detail=":: installing aquamarine (0.15.0-2) breaks dependency 'libaquamarine.so=13-64' required by hyprland"
RESOLVE_DETAIL="$detail" run_update >"$test_tmp/out" 2>"$test_tmp/err" || true
if grep -q "held by IgnorePkg" "$test_tmp/err"; then
  cat "$test_tmp/err" >&2
  fail "an unsatisfiable dependency is blamed on an IgnorePkg hold that does not exist"
fi
pass "an unsatisfiable dependency with nothing held is not blamed on a hold"
```

Actual output at the reviewed head (last lines, colour codes stripped):

```
ok - a clean upgrade runs a single pacman transaction
error: failed to prepare transaction (could not satisfy dependencies)

A dependency this upgrade cannot satisfy stopped it:
:: installing aquamarine (0.15.0-2) breaks dependency 'libaquamarine.so=13-64' required by hyprland

A package held by IgnorePkg in /etc/pacman.conf still requires a version of
something this upgrade wants to replace. Either drop the hold so the two move
together, or hold the dependency at the version the held package was built
against. Until one of those happens, every system upgrade stops here.
not ok - an unsatisfiable dependency is blamed on an IgnorePkg hold that does not exist
test exit: 1
```

### 2. Real pacman, no hold configured

This script uses the real `pacman` (7.1) as an ordinary user against a throwaway root: no root, no network, and the system's package databases are not touched. The test `pacman.conf` has no `IgnorePkg`. The repository has a new `aquamarine` but has not rebuilt `hyprland` yet (the shape of issue #11086), and a foreign package was built against the old library. Run it as `bash repro_no_hold.sh <omarchy checkout at the PR head>`.

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Reproducer for PR #11692: the dependency branch blames an IgnorePkg hold even
# when pacman.conf has no IgnorePkg at all.
#
# Usage: repro_no_hold.sh <omarchy checkout at the PR head>
# Needs only bash, python3 and pacman. Runs as an ordinary user against a
# throwaway pacman root (no root, no network, host databases untouched).
set -euo pipefail
omarchy=$1
lab=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$lab"' EXIT
db=$lab/root/var/lib/pacman
mkdir -p "$db/local" "$db/sync" "$lab/bin" "$lab/root/cache" "$lab/root/gnupg" "$lab/root/hooks"
echo 9 >"$db/local/ALPM_DB_VERSION"

# Installed: hyprland built against libaquamarine.so=13, and a foreign (AUR)
# tool built against it too. No IgnorePkg anywhere.
local_pkg() { # name version depends/provides lines...
  mkdir -p "$db/local/$1-$2"
  printf '%%NAME%%\n%s\n\n%%VERSION%%\n%s\n\n%%ARCH%%\nany\n\n%s\n' "$1" "$2" "$3" >"$db/local/$1-$2/desc"
  printf '%%FILES%%\n\n' >"$db/local/$1-$2/files"
}
local_pkg hyprland 0.50.0-1 $'%DEPENDS%\nlibaquamarine.so=13-64'
local_pkg some-aur-tool 1.0-1 $'%DEPENDS%\nlibaquamarine.so=13-64'
local_pkg aquamarine 0.14.0-1 $'%PROVIDES%\nlibaquamarine.so=13-64'

# The repository has the new aquamarine but has not rebuilt hyprland yet
# (the shape of issue #11086, a fresh install with no hold).
python3 - "$db/sync/core.db" <<'PY'
import io, sys, tarfile
pkgs = {
    'hyprland-0.50.0-1': 'hyprland\n\n%VERSION%\n0.50.0-1\n\n%DEPENDS%\nlibaquamarine.so=13-64\n',
    'aquamarine-0.15.0-2': 'aquamarine\n\n%VERSION%\n0.15.0-2\n\n%PROVIDES%\nlibaquamarine.so=14-64\n',
}
with tarfile.open(sys.argv[1], 'w:gz') as tf:
    for d, body in pkgs.items():
        data = (f'%FILENAME%\n{d}-any.pkg.tar.zst\n\n%NAME%\n' + body +
                '\n%ARCH%\nany\n\n%CSIZE%\n1\n\n%ISIZE%\n1\n').encode()
        ti = tarfile.TarInfo(d); ti.type = tarfile.DIRTYPE; ti.mode = 0o755; tf.addfile(ti)
        ti = tarfile.TarInfo(d + '/desc'); ti.size = len(data); tf.addfile(ti, io.BytesIO(data))
PY

cat >"$lab/pacman.conf" <<EOF
[options]
RootDir = $lab/root
DBPath = $db/
CacheDir = $lab/root/cache/
LogFile = $lab/root/pacman.log
GPGDir = $lab/root/gnupg/
HookDir = $lab/root/hooks/
Architecture = auto
SigLevel = Never

[core]
Server = file://$lab/nowhere
EOF
printf '#!/bin/bash\nexec /usr/bin/pacman --config %q "$@"\n' "$lab/pacman.conf" >"$lab/bin/pacman"
chmod +x "$lab/bin/pacman"

echo "== IgnorePkg lines in the test pacman.conf:"
grep -c IgnorePkg "$lab/pacman.conf" || true

# The verdict pacman puts on stderr is what omarchy-update-system-pkgs saves.
report=$lab/report
PATH="$lab/bin:$PATH" LC_ALL=C pacman -Sup --print-format '%n' 2>"$report" >/dev/null || true
echo "== pacman stderr (the report the handler receives):"
cat "$report"

echo "== handler output at the PR head:"
set +e
PATH="$lab/bin:$omarchy/bin:$PATH" OMARCHY_UPDATE_CONFLICT=1 \
  bash "$omarchy/bin/omarchy-update-system-pkgs-when-conflicted" "$report" 2>&1 |
  sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g'
echo "== handler exit: ${PIPESTATUS[0]}"
```

Actual output at the reviewed head:

```
== IgnorePkg lines in the test pacman.conf:
0
== pacman stderr (the report the handler receives):
error: failed to prepare transaction (could not satisfy dependencies)
== handler output at the PR head:

A dependency this upgrade cannot satisfy stopped it:
:: installing aquamarine (0.15.0-2) breaks dependency 'libaquamarine.so=13-64' required by hyprland
:: installing aquamarine (0.15.0-2) breaks dependency 'libaquamarine.so=13-64' required by some-aur-tool

A package held by IgnorePkg in /etc/pacman.conf still requires a version of
something this upgrade wants to replace. Either drop the hold so the two move
together, or hold the dependency at the version the held package was built
against. Until one of those happens, every system upgrade stops here.
== handler exit: 1
```
</details>

<details><summary>Details</summary>

**Verified:**
- The caller captures only stderr, and pacman prints the verdict on stderr and the `::` lines on stdout (`src/pacman/sync.c`, `util.c` in pacman 7.1).
- `pacman -Sup` as an ordinary user reprints the same `::` lines, needs no root or lock, and leaves no `db.lck`.
- The new branch cannot catch a conflict report (pacman fails with either conflicting or unsatisfied dependencies in one run), and it neither retries nor moves files.
- The new tests pass at the head, and the first fails against the base handler.

**Optional test improvement:** the second new case passes against the base handler when run on its own, and removing both `grep '^::'` and `2>/dev/null` from the re-run still passes the file. A stub that also prints an `error:` line on stderr and a non-`::` line on stdout would pin the filter if the case also asserts that those lines do not reach the output.

**Related open PRs:** #13538, #13601 and #9285 each change the same spot in this handler and conflict textually with this PR (#9285 also in the test file). If #13538 lands first, this branch has to stay above its `exists in filesystem ... || exit 1` line to stay reachable. #9070 (which currently conflicts with the `quattro` base branch) deletes this handler entirely.
</details>
